q1.question: Does Musterli cost anything?
q1.answer: No. Every generator, converter and export is free, without limits. Musterli is funded by voluntary donations.

q2.question: Do I need an account?
q2.answer: No. You can start right away. Sharing works with a link that contains your settings.

q3.question: Are my images uploaded?
q3.answer: No. Motifs, converters and the palette from an image run entirely in your browser. Your files are not sent to a server.

q4.question: Can I use the motifs commercially?
q4.answer: Yes. You may use whatever you export from Musterli freely, including commercially. We will publish the exact license text on this website.

q5.question: Which formats can I export?
q5.answer: Depending on the tool, SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP and CSS. Color tools also give you a Tailwind config and CSS variables.

css-gradient.name: CSS Gradient
css-gradient.description: Linear, radial and conic gradients with smooth OKLCH transitions. Export as CSS, SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: A CSS gradient is a color transition the browser draws itself. It needs no image file, loads instantly and stays sharp at any size. This generator mixes colors in the OKLCH color space, so transitions look even and avoid a muddy gray middle.
seo.howTo: Choose linear, radial or conic, set your colors and adjust angle, center and easing. Press Space for new variations. When you are happy, copy the CSS or the Tailwind classes, or export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.

q1.question: Why OKLCH instead of sRGB?
q1.answer: In sRGB many color pairs pass through a dull, gray middle. OKLCH blends by perceived lightness and chroma, so transitions stay vivid. For older browsers the CSS also contains an sRGB gradient as a fallback.

q2.question: What do the extra stops do?
q2.answer: They add intermediate colors along the transition, so the gradient follows the chosen easing curve, such as ease in and out, instead of running linearly.

q3.question: Can I use the gradient with Tailwind?
q3.answer: Yes. Next to the CSS, the export offers ready-made Tailwind classes you can paste straight into your markup.

q4.question: Does the exported image match the preview?
q4.answer: Yes. For SVG and images the same gradient is drawn as a vector graphic, at the size you choose in the export dialog.

css-patterns.name: CSS Patterns
css-patterns.description: Over 30 pure CSS patterns: dots, grids, stripes, waves and geometric shapes. Export as CSS, Tailwind, SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: CSS patterns are backgrounds the browser draws itself from gradients. They need no image file, load instantly, stay sharp at any size and can be recolored with a few characters of CSS. The library contains over 30 original patterns in five categories.
seo.howTo: Pick a pattern, set size, colors and opacity, and rotate stripes or grids to the angle you need. Stack up to five patterns as layers, show or hide them and change their order. Press Space for new variations. When you are happy, copy the CSS or the Tailwind classes, or export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.

q1.question: Do the patterns need an image?
q1.answer: No. Every pattern is made only of CSS gradients in background-image. That saves loading time and stays sharp on every screen.

q2.question: Which browsers support the patterns?
q2.answer: All current browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. The patterns use linear, radial and conic gradients, which have been widely supported for years.

q3.question: How exact is the SVG export?
q3.answer: The SVG redraws the same geometry with SVG gradients and tiles. At most, antialiasing of single pixels may differ. For an image without any deviation, use the PNG export.

q4.question: Can I use the patterns with Tailwind?
q4.answer: Yes. The export gives you Tailwind classes with arbitrary values that you paste straight into your HTML. They work with Tailwind 3 and 4.

q5.question: May I use the patterns commercially?
q5.answer: Yes. What you create with Musterli is yours and may be used in personal and commercial projects.

blob.name: Blob Generator
blob.description: Organic shapes in one click, filled, outlined or with a gradient. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: Blobs are soft, organic shapes. They loosen up strict layouts and work as backgrounds, photo frames or accents behind text. Each shape starts as a few points on a circle that are nudged at random and joined with smooth curves.
seo.howTo: Set complexity, randomness and size, then pick a fill: solid, outline or gradient. Press Space until you like the shape. Export as SVG, as an image or as a CSS clip-path to crop photos into a blob.

q1.question: How do I get the same shape again?
q1.answer: Every shape depends on the seed and the settings. Share or bookmark the link from the editor and the exact same shape appears when you open it.

q2.question: Can I crop a photo into a blob shape?
q2.answer: Yes. Export the shape as a clip-path and apply the CSS to your image. The shape scales with the element.

q3.question: Does the SVG have a background?
q3.answer: No, the background is transparent by default, so the blob sits on any surface without visible edges.

q4.question: How many points does a blob have?
q4.answer: That is what complexity controls. Few points give calm, round shapes, many points give lively, playful outlines.

svg-waves.name: SVG Waves
svg-waves.description: Layered waves for sections, headers and backgrounds. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

seo.whatIs: SVG waves are lightweight vector graphics that softly separate the sections of a website. Instead of a hard edge, one surface flows into the next. Several layers in graded colors add depth while the file stays just a few kilobytes.
seo.howTo: Choose the number of layers and points, set amplitude, smoothness and coverage, and decide whether the waves rise from the bottom or hang from the top. Press Space for new variations. Export as SVG, CSS background or image.

q1.question: How do I place a wave between two sections?
q1.answer: Download the SVG and put it at the bottom of the upper section. Use the background color of the next section as the wave color and both blend seamlessly.

q2.question: Does the wave stay sharp on wide screens?
q2.answer: Yes. As a vector graphic it scales without losing quality. Set its width to 100 percent in CSS and let the height follow.

q3.question: What does smoothness do?
q3.answer: It sets how softly the curve runs between points. Low smoothness gives jagged, mountain-like shapes, high smoothness calm, rounded waves.

q4.question: Can I flip the waves?
q4.answer: Yes. The direction setting decides whether the waves rise from the bottom or come down from the top.

polka-dots.name: Polka Dots
polka-dots.description: Dot patterns on a grid, offset or freely scattered. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: Polka dots are dot patterns, evenly spaced or freely scattered. Depending on size and color they look playful or calm, and they suit backgrounds for websites, packaging, cards and fabrics. Besides circles you can use rings and squares.
seo.howTo: Pick a layout (grid, offset or scatter), set spacing and dot size, and choose whether dots share one color, alternate or get random colors. Press Space for new variations. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: What is the difference between grid and offset?
q1.answer: In a grid the dots sit in straight rows and columns. Offset shifts every other row by half a step, which looks denser and more classic.

q2.question: How do I keep scattered dots from overlapping?
q2.answer: With the scatter layout the dots keep a minimum distance based on the spacing. Add size variation for extra variety.

q3.question: Can I use the pattern as a CSS background?
q3.answer: Yes. The CSS export embeds the pattern as SVG, so you can use it directly as a background-image.

q4.question: Which shapes are available?
q4.answer: Circles, rings and squares. Rings feel lighter and work well for bright, airy backgrounds.

geometric-patterns.name: Geometric Patterns
geometric-patterns.description: Grids of tiles with geometric shapes, even or nested. Edit any single tile, export as SVG, CSS or image.

seo.whatIs: A geometric pattern is a grid of tiles, each holding one simple shape: circles, quarter circles, triangles, stars or arcs. Rotation and color changes turn a handful of shapes into lively surfaces, familiar from Bauhaus posters, tiles and quilts. Such patterns work well for website backgrounds, slides, packaging and social media graphics.
seo.howTo: Pick a shape pack or put together your own shapes. Set the number of tiles per row, choose an even or nested grid and how shapes rotate. Color the tiles at random from your palette or per shape layer, with or without tile fills. Press the space bar for new variations. Click a tile to change its shape, color and rotation. Export as SVG, as a CSS background or as an image.

q1.question: Can I change single tiles?
q1.answer: Yes. Click a tile in the preview, or reach it with Tab and the arrow keys and press Enter. The popup lets you swap shape, color and rotation. Edited tiles survive new variations and travel with share links and saved designs.

q2.question: What is the difference between an even and a nested grid?
q2.answer: Even means all tiles have the same size. In a nested grid every tile splits into four smaller ones with the chance you choose, up to four levels deep. The result is a mosaic of large and small tiles.

q3.question: Does the pattern tile seamlessly?
q3.answer: Yes. The grid always fills the canvas with whole tiles, so the full design repeats without a visible edge. The CSS export uses it as a background with background-repeat.

q4.question: What are the tile shapes and quarter turns for?
q4.answer: The shapes of the “Tiles and quarters” pack meet the tile edges at fixed points. With quarter turns neighbouring tiles connect, which creates mazes and arc patterns in the spirit of Truchet tiles.

q5.question: May I use the patterns freely?
q5.answer: Yes. Musterli drew every shape itself. You can use your exports privately and commercially, without an account and without watermarks.

seamless-patterns.name: Seamless Patterns
seamless-patterns.description: Seamlessly tiling patterns made of shapes or your own graphic. Export as SVG, CSS, tile or image.

seo.whatIs: A seamless pattern is a tile that repeats any number of times without visible edges. Motifs that cross the border reappear on the opposite side, so the joins disappear. Seamless patterns work well for website backgrounds, wrapping paper, fabric, wallpaper and packaging.
seo.howTo: Pick one of the built-in shapes or load your own SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP file and crop it. Choose the tiling (grid, brick, half drop or mirror), size, spacing and rotation, and color the motifs with one color or a palette. Press the space bar for new variations. Export as SVG, as a CSS background, as a single PNG tile or as an image.

q1.question: Is my uploaded file stored or shared?
q1.answer: No. Your file is processed only in your browser, never sent to a server and never put into links. Anyone opening your link sees the pattern with the chosen shape.

q2.question: What is the difference between brick and half drop?
q2.answer: Brick shifts every other row by half a tile width, like a brick wall. Half drop shifts every other column by half a tile height instead.

q3.question: How do I use the pattern as a CSS background?
q3.answer: The CSS export contains the tile as an embedded SVG together with background-size and background-repeat. Paste the code into your element's rule and the pattern repeats seamlessly.

q4.question: Why is my SVG file a single color?
q4.answer: Unless Keep original colors is on, Musterli recolors the graphic with your motif color or palette. Turn the option on to keep the file's own colors.

q5.question: Why were parts of my SVG file removed?
q5.answer: For safety, Musterli only lets plain graphic elements through. Scripts, embedded web content, fonts and references to other files are removed.

noise-grain.name: Noise and Grain
noise-grain.description: Grainy textures and backgrounds with fine noise over a color or gradient. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG.

seo.whatIs: Grain is fine random noise on top of a surface. It takes the sterile smoothness out of digital colors and gradients, hides banding in gradients and evokes analog film or paper.
seo.howTo: Pick a color or gradient as the base, adjust amount, grain size and blend mode, and press Space for a new variant. Then export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG at the size you need.

faq.q1: Which blend mode should I use?
faq.a1: Overlay brightens light areas and darkens dark ones for a punchy grain. Soft light is gentler. Multiply only darkens and suits paper looks and light surfaces.
faq.q2: How do I get a transparent grain texture?
faq.a2: Set the base to Transparent and export as PNG or WebP. The file then holds only the grain, ready to place over images in other apps.
faq.q3: Does the export look the same as the preview?
faq.a3: Yes. Preview and export use the same graphic, and the noise is computed from the seed. The same settings and seed always give the same grain, in every browser.
faq.a4: The grain is a seamless 256 pixel tile. With fine grain the repeat is practically invisible, and the file stays small.

grid-patterns.name: Grid Patterns
grid-patterns.description: Grid lines, dot grids, crosses or tiles with major and minor grids. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: Grid patterns are regular grids of lines, dots, crosses or tiles. They evoke graph paper, blueprints or dotted notebooks and make a calm background for websites, slides and product shots.
seo.howTo: Pick a style, set the cell size and weight, and choose whether every n-th line is highlighted as a major grid. Use the fade to soften the grid towards the center or the edges. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: Does the grid keep its look when I resize?
q1.answer: Yes. The cell size is a percentage of the shorter edge, so the grid looks equally dense in every format.

q2.question: What is the major grid?
q2.answer: Every n-th line (or dot) is drawn thicker and in the second color, just like graph paper. Set it to 0 to turn it off.

q3.question: Can I tile the grid seamlessly?
q3.answer: The grid is centered on the canvas. For seamless tiles, use a size that is a multiple of the cell size and turn off the fade.

q4.question: Does the SVG work in Figma and Illustrator?
q4.answer: Yes. Lines are stored as paths and the fade uses a standard SVG mask that both apps can read.

confetti.name: Confetti
confetti.description: Confetti made of strips, circles, triangles and squiggles, evenly spread. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: The confetti generator spreads colorful shapes evenly yet naturally across the canvas. Great for invitations, birthday graphics, social posts and festive backgrounds.
seo.howTo: Pick a shape or a mix, set spacing, size and rotation, and choose your colors. Press Space for new variations. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: Why don't the pieces overlap?
q1.answer: Positions come from Poisson-disk sampling: every piece keeps a minimum distance, so the spread looks even but still random.

q2.question: How do I get a different arrangement with the same settings?
q2.answer: Press Space or change the seed. Your settings stay, only positions, shapes and colors are reshuffled.

q3.question: Can I use a single shape?
q3.answer: Yes. Choose only circles or only squiggles instead of the mix.

q4.question: Is the SVG editable?
q4.answer: Yes. Every piece is a plain path or circle without transforms, grouped by color.

starry-sky.name: Starry Sky
starry-sky.description: A starry night sky with a color gradient, twinkling stars and sparkles. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: The starry sky generator creates a night sky from a color gradient and many stars of different size and brightness. Perfect for backgrounds, picture book art, event graphics and wallpapers.
seo.howTo: Set the sky colors from top to bottom, adjust star spacing, size and brightness variation, and add glow and a few sparkles if you like. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: How are the stars distributed?
q1.answer: With Poisson-disk sampling. Stars keep a minimum distance, so the sky looks natural without clumps or gaps.

q2.question: Why are there more small stars than large ones?
q2.answer: Star sizes are drawn so that small stars are more common, which matches how a real night sky looks.

q3.question: What are sparkles?
q3.answer: A few larger four-pointed stars that act as highlights. Set them to 0 to turn them off.

q4.question: Can I use it as a desktop wallpaper?
q4.answer: Yes. Pick a desktop size such as Full HD or 4K and export as PNG.

dieter-dots.name: Dieter Dots
dieter-dots.description: Concentric rings of dots, like a perforated speaker grille. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: Dieter Dots are dots arranged in concentric rings around the center, inspired by perforated speaker grilles in industrial design. The pattern feels technical and calm and suits posters, covers and product graphics.
seo.howTo: Set the number of rings, the dots in the first ring and the ring spacing. Twist turns the rings into a spiral, shrink outwards fades the dots towards the edge. Choose one color, alternating rings or a gradient, then export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: Why do outer rings have more dots?
q1.answer: Each ring gets as many dots as needed to keep the spacing along the ring equal to the first ring. Ring 3 has three times as many dots as ring 1.

q2.question: Why do I see fewer rings than I set?
q2.answer: Rings outside the canvas are skipped, and we draw at most 10,000 dots per image to keep the browser responsive.

q3.question: Can I make a spiral?
q3.answer: Yes. Increase the twist and each ring is rotated a bit further than the previous one.

blob-composition.name: Blob Composition
blob-composition.description: Several blobs at corners and edges that adapt to any canvas size. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: A blob composition arranges several organic shapes as layers at the corners and edges of a canvas. The result is a calm background for websites, slides and social posts that keeps the center free for text.
seo.howTo: Pick a preset or press Space for new arrangements. For each blob, set position, offset, size and shape, move layers up or down and hide them. Colors are taken from your palette in order. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: What happens when I change the canvas size?
q1.answer: Positions are stored relative to the corners and edges, sizes relative to the shorter side. The composition adapts to every format, from square to wide banner.

q2.question: How do I change the color of a single blob?
q2.answer: The top blob uses the first palette color, the second blob the second color and so on. Change the palette or reorder the blobs.

q3.question: Does a blob keep its shape when I change the others?
q3.answer: Yes. Each shape depends only on its own shape variant, complexity and randomness. Use the lock to keep single values when you randomize.

q4.question: How many blobs can I add?
q4.answer: Up to eight layers. Two to four usually make the calmest backgrounds.

doodles.name: Doodle Backgrounds
doodles.description: Hand-drawn looking squiggles, spirals, stars and zigzags as a background. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: Doodle backgrounds are made of small shapes that look drawn by hand: squiggles, spirals, stars, crosses and zigzags. They feel playful and personal and work well for invitations, school and kids themes, social posts and packaging.
seo.howTo: Pick a shape or the mix, set spacing, size and stroke width, and use wobble to decide how hand-drawn the lines look. Press Space for new variations and export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: Why do the lines look hand-drawn?
q1.answer: Every point of a shape is shifted slightly with smooth noise, then the points are joined with soft curves and drawn with round line caps.

q2.question: Where do the shapes come from?
q2.answer: All shapes are generated in your browser from simple geometric rules. There are no image templates, every variation is new.

q3.question: Why don't the doodles overlap?
q3.answer: Positions come from Poisson-disk sampling. Every shape keeps a minimum distance, so the spread looks even yet random.

q4.question: Can I edit the SVG?
q4.answer: Yes. All strokes of one color sit in a single stroked path without transforms, easy to recolor in Figma or Illustrator.

svg-charts.name: SVG Charts
svg-charts.description: Placeholder charts with random data for mockups: lines, areas and bars. Export as SVG or image.

seo.whatIs: SVG charts are placeholder charts with random data. Use them in mockups, slides, landing pages and app designs when real numbers are missing or must not be shown.
seo.howTo: Choose line, area or bars, set the number of series and data points, and adjust trend and volatility. Turn axes and grid lines on or off. Press Space for new data. Export as SVG, CSS or image.

q1.question: Can I enter my own data?
q1.answer: No, the tool generates random data for drafts on purpose. Trend and volatility control whether the curve rises, falls or swings.

q2.question: Why are there no labels?
q2.answer: Without text the SVG looks the same in every app and needs no fonts. Add labels in your layout, for example in Figma.

q3.question: Does the data stay when I change the style?
q3.answer: Yes. The data depends on the seed. You can change chart type, colors, axes and smoothing without changing the values.

q4.question: How do I get new random data?
q4.answer: Press Space. Type, series and style stay, data, trend and colors are reshuffled. Use the lock to keep single values.

palette-generator.name: Color Palette Generator
palette-generator.description: Harmonious color palettes at the press of the space bar. Lock colors, pick a harmony, check contrast and export as CSS.

harmony.label: Harmony
harmony.description: Recolours all unlocked colours right away. Press the space bar for a new palette in the same harmony.

matrix.label: Contrast matrix
matrix.description: Shows every color as text on every other color with its contrast ratio.

seo.whatIs: A color palette generator puts together colors that work well with each other. Musterli works in the OKLCH color space, so lightness and hue steps look even to the eye.
seo.howTo: Press the space bar for a new palette. Lock the colors you like, choose a harmony and export the palette as CSS variables, a HEX list or an image.

faq.a1: Analogous uses neighboring hues, complementary uses opposite ones. Triadic spreads three hues evenly, split complementary pairs a hue with the neighbors of its opposite, and tetradic uses four hues in a square.
faq.a2: Locked colors stay when you shuffle. The first locked color acts as the anchor, and the new palette is built around it in the chosen harmony.
faq.q3: What does the contrast display show?
faq.a3: The WCAG 2 contrast ratio between each color and its label. AA means at least 4.5:1, AAA at least 7:1 for normal text.
faq.q4: Can I use the palette in Figma or in code?
faq.a4: Yes. Copy the HEX list or the CSS variables, or export the palette as SVG or PNG.

tints-shades.name: Tints & Shades
tints-shades.description: Lighter and darker steps of a color. Export as HEX, RGB, HSL or CSS variables.

method.label: Method
method.description: OKLCH keeps the colorfulness, mixing moves evenly towards white or black.

seo.whatIs: Tints are lighter versions of a color, shades are darker ones. Together they form a scale for hover states, backgrounds and borders.
seo.howTo: Pick a base color, set the number of tints and shades and copy the values as HEX, RGB, HSL or CSS variables.

faq.q1: What is the difference between a tint and a shade?
faq.a1: A tint is a color mixed with white, a shade is a color mixed with black.
faq.a2: The OKLCH method only changes lightness and keeps the colorfulness, so steps stay vivid. Mixing in OKLab looks even, mixing in sRGB matches classic tools like Sass.
faq.q3: How do I use the CSS variables?
faq.a3: Paste the block into your stylesheet and use the colors with var(), for example var(--primary-tint-2).

tailwind-palette.name: Tailwind Color Palette
tailwind-palette.description: The eleven Tailwind steps 50 to 950 from one color. Export for tailwind.config.js, @theme, OKLCH and HEX.

seo.whatIs: Tailwind CSS arranges every color in eleven steps from 50 (very light) to 950 (very dark). This generator builds such a scale from your brand color, with the color itself exactly on 500.
seo.howTo: Pick your base color, give the palette a name and copy the code for tailwind.config.js or the @theme block for Tailwind v4.

faq.q1: Does it work with Tailwind v4?
faq.a1: Yes. The @theme export creates variables like --color-brand-500 in OKLCH, just like Tailwind v4 uses them. For older versions there is the tailwind.config.js export.
faq.a2: Step 500 is the main color in Tailwind. The lighter and darker steps follow a lightness curve modeled on well-known UI palettes.
faq.q3: Why are the ends less saturated?
faq.a3: Very light and very dark colors quickly look garish or muddy at full saturation. The slider sets how much the saturation drops.
faq.a4: OKLCH describes colors by lightness, chroma and hue the way the eye perceives them. Modern browsers understand OKLCH directly in CSS.

palette-from-image.name: Palette from Image
palette-from-image.description: Drop in a photo and get its main colors with their share in percent. The image stays in your browser.

count.label: Number of colors
count.description: How many main colors to look for in the image.

seo.whatIs: Palette from Image finds the colors that define a photo or graphic and shows how much of the area each one covers. The analysis runs entirely in your browser: your image is never uploaded and never stored.
seo.howTo: Drop an image onto the drop zone, paste it with Ctrl+V or choose a file (PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG up to 5 MB). Set the number of colors, press the space bar for another grouping and export the palette as a HEX list, CSS variables, Tailwind or an image.

faq.a1: No. The image is scaled down and analyzed in your browser. It never leaves your device, is not part of shared links and is not stored.
faq.a2: Musterli groups the pixels with k-means in the OKLab color space, which measures color differences the way the eye sees them. Each group becomes one color, and its share is the area it covers in the image.
faq.q3: Why does the space bar change the palette?
faq.a3: k-means starts from randomly chosen colors and can settle on slightly different groups depending on the start. The space bar tries a new start, so you can keep the variant you like best.
faq.q4: Why does a shared link show the sample image?
faq.a4: Shared links contain only the settings, never your image or the colors taken from it. Whoever opens the link sees the sample image and can drop in their own. To pass on the colors, export them as a HEX list or an image.
faq.a5: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF (first frame of an animation) and SVG up to 5 MB. Transparent pixels are not counted.

mesh-gradient.name: Mesh Gradient
mesh-gradient.description: Soft, flowing color gradients from several blurred color fields. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS.

seo.whatIs: A mesh gradient blends several colors across a surface instead of along a single line. The result looks like soft, flowing light and suits website heroes, app backgrounds, slides and social media posts.
seo.howTo: Pick your colors and a background, choose how many color fields to mix and how strongly to warp and blur them, and add some grain if you like. Press Space for a new arrangement. Then export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS in the size you need.

q1.question: How is a mesh gradient different from a normal gradient?
q1.answer: A linear or radial gradient runs along one line or out from one point. A mesh gradient places several colors freely on the surface and blends them softly, so it looks organic rather than technical.

q2.question: Can I edit the SVG in a design app?
q2.answer: The SVG contains plain shapes and one standard Gaussian blur filter, which browsers and many design apps can display. Support for SVG filters varies between editing apps, so if the blur looks different there, use the PNG export.

q3.question: Why is there grain on the gradient?
q3.answer: Fine grain gives the surface a soft, analog look and hides banding, the visible steps in smooth gradients. Set Grain to 0 for a perfectly smooth result.

q4.question: Does the export look like the preview?
q4.answer: Yes. Preview and export use the same graphic, and the arrangement is computed from the seed. The same settings and seed always give the same gradient.

blurry-gradient.name: Blurry Gradient
blurry-gradient.description: Dreamy backgrounds from large, strongly blurred color circles. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS.

seo.whatIs: A blurry gradient is a background made of a few large color circles, blurred so strongly that only soft clouds of color remain. It works well behind text, as a website hero, in presentations and as a wallpaper.
seo.howTo: Choose two to five circles and whether they sit in the corners or around the center, then set size, spread, opacity and blur. Press Space for a new variant, add grain if you like, and export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS.

q1.question: Will text stay readable on top?
q1.answer: Yes, with enough contrast. Light circles on a light background or dark ones on a dark background keep the surface calm. Lower the opacity if the colors compete with your text.

q2.question: Does the SVG use filters?
q2.answer: No. Every blurred circle is a radial gradient whose transparency follows the exact shape of a blurred circle. That is why the SVG looks the same in every browser and design app and renders fast at any size.

q3.question: What does Spread do?
q3.answer: It moves each circle away from its anchor point by a random amount, toward the middle of the image. At 0 the circles sit exactly on the corners or in the center.

q4.question: Does the export look like the preview?
q4.answer: Yes. Preview and export use the same graphic, and the positions are computed from the seed. The same settings and seed always give the same result.

striped-gradient.name: Striped Gradient
striped-gradient.description: Vertical stripes, each with its own gradient, slightly offset against each other. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS.

seo.whatIs: A striped gradient splits a color gradient into vertical bands and shifts each band a little. It looks like light through ribbed glass or folded fabric and makes a striking background for covers, posters and websites.
seo.howTo: Set your colors from top to bottom, then choose the number of stripes, how much their widths vary and how far they are offset. Shading adds light and shadow to every stripe. Press Space for new variants and export as PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or CSS.

q1.question: What does Offset do?
q1.answer: Every stripe runs through the same colors but starts at a slightly different height. The higher the offset, the more the stripes are out of step. At 0 they line up into one continuous gradient.

q2.question: How do I get a fluted glass look?
q2.answer: Use many narrow stripes, a small offset and strong shading. The Fluted glass preset is a good starting point.

q3.question: Is the SVG easy to edit?
q3.answer: Yes. Apart from the optional grain it consists only of rectangles with linear gradients, without filters, so design apps such as Figma, Illustrator or Inkscape open it as editable shapes.

q4.question: Does the export look like the preview?
q4.answer: Yes. Preview and export use the same graphic, and the offsets are computed from the seed. The same settings and seed always give the same result.

glass-effects.name: Glass and Border Effects
glass-effects.description: Frosted glass, gradient borders and glows for cards and hero sections. Real CSS with a live preview, ready to copy as CSS, Tailwind or HTML.

backgroundImage.label: Own background picture
backgroundImage.description: Replaces the stage with your picture (PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG). It stays in your browser, share links leave it out and the code points to a placeholder.

embedImage.label: Embed picture in the code
embedImage.description: Writes the picture into the code as a data URI instead of a placeholder. The code gets much longer.

advisories.textContrast: Text on the glass only reaches a contrast of {ratio}:1, WCAG AA needs {required}:1. Try a stronger tint or another text color.
advisories.imageContrast: With your own picture, Musterli cannot check the contrast of the text. Check it yourself, for example with a stronger tint.

seo.whatIs: Glass and border effects are CSS surfaces for cards, dialogs and hero sections: frosted glass with backdrop-filter, borders with a gradient (rotating if you like) and colored glows. The tool shows the effect as real CSS on a Musterli background and gives you the code.
seo.howTo: Pick glass, gradient border or glow. For glass, set blur, tint, saturation, inner border and grain; for the border, its colors, width and rotation; for the glow, its color, reach and strength. Switch the background under Stage. Press Space for new variations. Copy CSS, Tailwind classes or an HTML example.

q1.question: Does the glass effect work in Safari?
q1.answer: Yes. The code also writes backdrop-filter with the -webkit- prefix, which Safari needs before version 18. Chrome, Edge and Firefox support backdrop-filter without a prefix.

q2.question: Why is there no PNG of the glass?
q2.answer: Glass blurs whatever lies behind it on your page. An image would only capture the background in this tool. Gradient borders and glows can be exported as PNG or WebP.

q3.question: What happens to the rotating border with reduced motion?
q3.answer: People who ask their system for less motion see a still border: the code includes a prefers-reduced-motion rule. Browsers without @property show the static border too.

q4.question: Is text on glass readable?
q4.answer: That depends on the tint and the background. The tool checks the contrast of your text color on the tinted glass and shows a hint when it misses WCAG AA at 4.5:1.

bento-grid.name: Bento Grid
bento-grid.description: Rounded tiles of different sizes in a grid, without gaps. For feature sections, portfolios and social graphics, as CSS Grid, Tailwind or an image.

layoutSeed.label: Layout no.
layoutSeed.description: Every number gives another layout. Lock it to keep the layout while Space only rolls new colors.

breakpointColumns.label: Columns on narrow screens
breakpointColumns.description: Below 768 px the code arranges the tiles in reading order in this many columns.

backgroundImage.label: Grid background picture
backgroundImage.description: Sits behind all tiles. Stays in your browser, share links leave it out.

seo.whatIs: A bento grid arranges content in tiles of different sizes, like the compartments of a bento box. The layout is popular for feature sections, portfolios, dashboards and social media graphics. The generator always fills the whole grid, without gaps.
seo.howTo: Set columns, rows and the number of tiles you want. The smallest and largest tile control how varied the tiles get. Press Space for a new layout, or lock the layout and roll new colors only. Export as CSS Grid with HTML, Tailwind classes, SVG or an image.

q1.question: Can I move single tiles?
q1.answer: No, Musterli is deliberately not a layout editor. Roll layouts until one fits and lock it. Columns, rows and tile sizes are set with the controls.

q2.question: Does the grid work on phones?
q2.answer: Yes. Below 768 px the CSS arranges the tiles in reading order in fewer columns. Set how many under Columns on narrow screens.

q3.question: Are there gaps in the grid?
q3.answer: Never. The grid is split along cell lines until it has the number of tiles you asked for. Every cell belongs to exactly one tile.

q4.question: Do I need Tailwind for the code?
q4.answer: No. The CSS Grid + HTML export works in any browser without a framework. The Tailwind classes are an alternative for projects that use Tailwind.

q5.question: Can I put text, icons and pictures into the tiles?
q5.answer: Yes. Click a tile in the preview, or pick it with Tab and the arrow keys. You can set a title, a subtitle, an icon, your own graphic and a background picture. Pictures stay in your browser: share links leave them out, and the code points to placeholder files you replace with your pictures.

contrast-checker.name: Contrast Checker
contrast-checker.description: Check whether text and background are readable under WCAG, see the colors with color vision deficiency and apply better colors in one click.

sample.label: Sample
sample.description: Decides which levels count: body text needs 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA, large text 3:1 and 4.5:1, UI components 3:1.

simulation.label: Simulate color vision deficiency
simulation.description: Also shows the pair as people with a color vision deficiency see it, including its contrast.

pairs.label: All pairs of a palette
pairs.description: Shows every palette color as text on every other one, with its contrast ratio.

seo.whatIs: A contrast checker measures how much text and background colors differ in lightness. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2) set minimum ratios so text stays readable with low vision, glare or poor screens.
seo.howTo: Pick the text and background colors with the color picker, a HEX value or the eyedropper and read which WCAG levels pass. If the contrast falls short, apply the nearest color that reaches AA or AAA in one click. The simulation shows how the pair looks with color vision deficiency.

faq.q1: What do AA and AAA mean?
faq.a1: AA is the usual minimum: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. AAA is stricter and asks for 7:1 and 4.5:1. UI components and graphics need 3:1.
faq.a2: From 18 point (24 px) in regular weight or from 14 point (about 18.7 px) in bold.
faq.q3: Why does Musterli round the contrast down?
faq.a3: So a value that just misses never looks like a pass. Musterli shows 4.49:1 as 4.4:1, because under WCAG it is not enough for AA.
faq.q4: How does the color vision simulation work?
faq.a4: Musterli converts the colors with the published matrices by Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009); achromatopsia keeps only the lightness. The simulation is an approximation and does not replace testing with affected people.
faq.q5: How does Musterli find a better color?
faq.a5: It only moves the lightness in the OKLCH color space and keeps hue and chroma as far as possible. Your brand color stays recognizable and still reaches AA or AAA.

css-shadow.name: CSS Shadow Generator
css-shadow.description: Soft, layered shadows for cards and buttons. Real CSS preview, export as box-shadow, Tailwind or drop-shadow.

angle.label: Light direction
angle.description: Where the light comes from. At 0° it comes from the top and the shadow falls down.

autoColor.label: Color from background
autoColor.description: Darkens the hue of the background instead of using pure black. That looks more natural.

easing.label: Easing
easing.description: How distance and blur grow from layer to layer.

stage.label: Stage
stage.description: A Musterli background for the preview. It is not part of the CSS export.

seo.whatIs: A CSS shadow generator writes the code for box-shadow. Instead of one hard shadow, Musterli stacks several layers whose distance and blur grow along a curve. Cards and buttons look soft and naturally lit.
seo.howTo: Set layers, distance, blur and light direction, or press Space for a new variant. The preview is real CSS on a Musterli background. Then copy the box-shadow, the Tailwind class, the @theme variable or the drop-shadow version.

faq.a1: A real shadow is dark and sharp close to the object and gets lighter and softer further away. Several layers recreate that, while a single box-shadow often looks flat or muddy.
faq.q2: How do I use the shadow in Tailwind?
faq.a2: For Tailwind v3 and v4 there is the class shadow-[...] with all layers. In Tailwind v4 you can also store the shadow as a --shadow-name variable in @theme and simply write shadow-name.
faq.q3: What is the difference to drop-shadow?
faq.a3: box-shadow follows the element's rectangle, filter: drop-shadow() follows its shape, for example of a cut-out PNG or SVG. drop-shadow has no spread and no inner shadow.
faq.q4: Why is the shadow not black?
faq.a4: Shadows pick up some of the color around them. That is why Musterli darkens the hue of the background by default. You can still pick your own color.

guilloche.name: Guilloche
guilloche.description: Fine interlaced line work like on banknotes and certificates: rosettes, borders and frames. Export as SVG, image or GIF.

inner.label: Inner edge
inner.description: Rosette and frame: distance from the center relative to half the shorter edge. Band: height above the bottom edge relative to the image height.

outer.label: Outer edge
outer.description: Rosette and frame: distance from the center relative to half the shorter edge. Band: height above the bottom edge relative to the image height.

petals.label: Petals
petals.description: How often the base shape appears per turn or per repeat.

frequency.label: Swings
frequency.description: How often every line swings between the edges per turn or per repeat.

spread.label: Offset
spread.description: How far the lines are shifted against each other. At 1 they are spread evenly.

colorMode.label: Coloring
colorMode.description: Blend: each line in one color, spread across the lines. Iris print: one gradient across the whole image. Along: the color changes along every line.

seo.whatIs: Guilloche is the name for fine, interlaced line patterns as you know them from banknotes, share certificates, diplomas and vouchers. They used to be engraved into metal with rose engine lathes; today they come from simple formulas: lines swinging between two edges, spirographs made of rotating pointers and overlaid sine waves. The generator computes everything right in your browser.
seo.howTo: Pick a layout: rosette for a seal or watermark, band for a tileable border, or frame for the edge of a certificate. Then set the curve, the number of lines, petals and swings, place the inner and outer edge and choose colors, including an iris print or a blend along the lines. Press the space bar for new variations. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP or as an animated GIF.

q1.question: Can I use the patterns for real banknotes or ID documents?
q1.answer: No. The patterns are decorative and offer no protection against counterfeiting. Use them for certificates, vouchers, invitations, labels, packaging or backgrounds.

q2.question: How do I make a border that repeats?
q2.answer: Choose the band layout and a wide, low format such as 1600 × 200 pixels. Set the inner edge close to 0 and the outer edge close to 1. The band joins seamlessly on the left and right, so you can place it side by side as often as you like.

q3.question: Why does my pattern look like a solid area?
q3.answer: With many lines and many swings the lines sit very close together. Reduce the number of lines or swings, or make the lines thinner.

q4.question: How large is the SVG file?
q4.answer: Curves are sampled just finely enough to look smooth and stored with one decimal place. Typical patterns are 50 to 250 KB; even extreme settings stay below about 1.5 MB.

q5.question: What does the animation show?
q5.answer: In a GIF export with motion, the phase of every line moves once all the way around. The pattern seems to flow, and the loop has no jump.

topo-lines.name: Topographic Lines
topo-lines.description: Contour lines like on a map, as outlines or filled elevation bands. Export as SVG, image or GIF.

majorEvery.label: Index line every
majorEvery.description: Every nth line is drawn wider, like the index contours of a map. 0 turns them off.

seo.whatIs: Contour lines connect points of equal height, just like on a hiking map. Musterli creates a random terrain from noise and draws its contours at even intervals. The result works as a calm background for websites, slides, posters or packaging and stays sharp as SVG.
seo.howTo: Shape the terrain with scale, detail levels, roughness and warp, and choose how many lines to draw. Show lines, filled elevation bands or both, and highlight every nth line as an index line. Press the space bar for a new terrain. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP or as a GIF in which the lines slowly move.

q1.question: Are the contour lines real map data?
q1.answer: No. The terrain comes from mathematical noise and is entirely made up. That means you can use the graphic without licensing questions, and every seed gives you a new landscape.

q2.question: How large is the SVG file?
q2.answer: With the default settings usually between 100 and 400 KB. Musterli simplifies the lines and rounds coordinates. Many lines, many detail levels and bands with lines make the file larger, but it always stays below about 1.5 MB.

q3.question: What does warp do?
q3.answer: It shifts the terrain through itself with a second layer of noise. Small values make the shapes more organic, large values give flowing patterns reminiscent of marble or wood grain.

q4.question: Can I use my brand colors?
q4.answer: Yes. With a brand palette from your Brand Kit the tool takes your colors for the lines or bands and picks the darkest color for the lines on top of the bands.

flow-field.name: Flow Fields
flow-field.description: Thousands of lines follow an invisible flow, like wind, water or hair. Export as SVG, image or GIF.

separation.label: Minimum distance
separation.description: Share of the line spacing that lines keep from each other. At 0 lines may touch and cross.

seo.whatIs: A flow field is a field of directions that gives every point of the canvas an angle. Let many lines follow it and you get images reminiscent of wind, currents, fur or silk. Musterli computes the field from noise or from swirls and can keep a minimum distance, so the lines never clump together.
seo.howTo: Pick the field, its scale and turbulence, then the start points, line spacing and length. Stroke shape, line width and opacity set the character, and the colors come from the palette, the direction or the position. Press the space bar for a new variation. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP or as a GIF with travelling strokes.

q1.question: What is the difference between noise and swirl?
q1.answer: With noise, the lines roughly follow a main direction and stray from it depending on the turbulence. The swirl field derives its directions from noise so that lines circle around and never converge in a single point.

q2.question: What is the minimum distance for?
q2.answer: A line stops as soon as it gets too close to another one, so the lines spread evenly across the canvas. At 0 they may overlap, which gives soft, hair-like textures at a low opacity.

q3.question: How large is the SVG file?
q3.answer: With the default settings usually below 300 KB. Musterli simplifies every line and rounds coordinates. The number of lines, steps and points is capped, so the file stays below about 1.5 MB and the preview stays responsive.

q4.question: What does the GIF animation look like?
q4.answer: With the motion source the lines turn into strokes that travel along the field, in a seamless loop. Alternatively the frames show new variations or cycle through the colors.

low-poly.name: Low Poly & Voronoi
low-poly.description: Faceted backgrounds from triangles or Voronoi cells, colored by a gradient through your palette. Export as SVG, image or GIF.

seo.whatIs: Low poly is a faceted look made of flat triangles, like a cut gem or a paper model. Voronoi cells split the surface into organic regions around scattered points, like dry earth or a mosaic. Both make striking backgrounds for websites, slides, posters and social posts.
seo.howTo: Pick triangles or Voronoi cells, set the point spacing and choose a gradient through your colors. Add light for a sculpted look, lines for a wireframe, or a gap and rounded corners for mosaic tiles. Press Space for a new arrangement. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, CSS or animated GIF.

q1.question: How are the triangles made?
q1.answer: Points are spread evenly with Poisson-disk sampling (or a jittered grid) and connected by a Delaunay triangulation: no triangle's circumcircle contains another point, which avoids thin slivers.

q2.question: What are Voronoi cells?
q2.answer: Each cell holds the part of the surface that is closer to its point than to any other point. The cells are clipped to the canvas, so the whole image is covered.

q3.question: Where do the colors come from?
q3.answer: Each face takes the color of the gradient at its center. Color variation and lighting change the brightness per face; lighting uses a random relief and the light direction you set.

q4.question: Can I animate it?
q4.answer: Yes. The GIF export can let the points drift on small loops (Motion), cycle the colors or show new arrangements.

q5.question: Is the SVG editable?
q5.answer: Yes. Every face is a plain path with its own fill color, without filters or transforms.

terrazzo.name: Terrazzo Pattern
terrazzo.description: Terrazzo surfaces with stone chips in several sizes, speckles and fine grain. Seamless tiles for CSS, or export as SVG and image.

seo.whatIs: Terrazzo is a floor and wall material made of stone and glass chips set in a binder and ground smooth. As a graphic it makes a lively, tactile pattern for packaging, websites, posters and product mockups.
seo.howTo: Choose angular chips, pebbles or a mix, then set the chip size, the number of size classes and how much of the surface they cover. Pick a base color and chip colors; the first color can dominate. Add speckles and grain for a natural finish. Keep Seamless tile on for patterns and export the tile as CSS or PNG, or the whole canvas as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.

q1.question: Do the chips overlap?
q1.answer: No. Each chip has a bounding circle, and a new chip is only placed where it keeps the set spacing to all others. Large chips come first, then medium and small ones fill the gaps.

q2.question: How does the seamless tile work?
q2.answer: Chips that cross an edge of the tile continue on the opposite side. The tile repeats in every direction without visible seams, as a CSS background or as a PNG tile.

q3.question: Can I use my brand colors?
q3.answer: Yes. Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit; the base color stays. The main color weight decides how often the first color appears.

q4.question: How large does the SVG get?
q4.answer: At most 2000 chips and 2500 speckles per tile. On very large surfaces the chips grow instead, so the SVG stays compact.

screenshot-beautifier.name: Screenshot Beautifier
screenshot-beautifier.description: Put your screenshot on a beautiful background or show your website as a mockup on laptop, monitor, tablet and phone. Ready for docs, social media and Product Hunt.

device.label: Device
device.description: Show your screenshot on its own or as a website mockup on one device or a responsive set of several.

screenshot.label: Your screenshot
screenshot.description: PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). For devices one screenshot is enough for all. It stays in your browser; share links leave it out.

screenshotTablet.label: Tablet screenshot
screenshotTablet.description: Optional. Without its own picture the tablet shows your screenshot, cropped to its screen from the top.

screenshotPhone.label: Phone screenshot
screenshotPhone.description: Optional. Without its own picture the phone shows the tablet screenshot or your main screenshot, cropped from the top.

align.label: Alignment
align.description: Where the window moves when it does not fill the format exactly.

theme.label: Color scheme
theme.description: Applies to the window bar and the placeholder.

url.label: Address or title
url.description: Shown in the bar, as text only. Stays on your device; share links leave it out.

live.label: Live view
live.description: Loads the address right inside the devices (https only). “Take this view” below the preview turns it into your picture. The website sees your IP address; Musterli does not.

highlight.label: Light edge
highlight.description: A fine light line along the inner edge, nice on dark windows.

advisories.liveUrl: The live view needs an https address, for example example.com.
advisories.url: This does not look like a web address. The bar still shows it as you typed it.

seo.whatIs: A screenshot beautifier turns a plain screen capture into a polished image. The picture sits on a background and gets padding, rounded corners, a soft shadow and, if you like, a window or browser bar with an address. Screenshots in documentation, blog posts, on social media and on Product Hunt look clean and consistent. As a website mockup it shows your page on a laptop, monitor, tablet or phone, and as a responsive mockup on several devices at once.
seo.howTo: Drop your screenshot into the editor, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V. Then pick a frame, padding, corners, shadow and a background: a color, a gradient or a Musterli background such as mesh, blurry or waves. Space rolls a new background and keeps your picture. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG, or copy the result straight to the clipboard. For a mockup, pick a laptop, monitor, tablet, phone or a responsive set under Device and type the address for the browser bar.

faq.a1: No. The picture is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links contain neither the picture nor the address in the bar. If you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.a2: PNG, JPG, WebP and SVG up to 5 MB. Raster pictures are scaled down to at most 3840 pixels on the long side and kept as PNG so text stays sharp. SVG is cleaned of scripts and external references first.
faq.q3: Which size fits Product Hunt, X or LinkedIn?
faq.a3: The size menu has ready formats: 1270 × 760 for Product Hunt, 1600 × 900 for X and slides, 1200 × 627 for LinkedIn and 1920 × 1200 for documentation. The screenshot adapts automatically.
faq.q4: What is in the SVG export?
faq.a4: Background, shadow and window bar are vectors; your screenshot is embedded as an image (data URI). The file needs nothing else but is about as large as your picture.
faq.q5: How do I make a responsive mockup of my website?
faq.a5: Choose “Responsive set” under Device. One screenshot is enough: every device shows it, cropped to its screen from the top. You can add separate screenshots for tablet and phone. With the live view your browser loads the website right into the devices, and “Take this view” turns it into pictures. Some websites do not allow embedding; then upload a screenshot.

svg-to-css.name: SVG to CSS
svg-to-css.title: SVG to CSS converter
svg-to-css.description: Turn SVG code into a CSS background with a compact, URL-encoded data URI.
svg-to-css.whatIs: A data URI embeds the SVG directly in your stylesheet, so the browser needs no extra request. URL encoding keeps the code shorter and more readable than Base64, which makes it the best choice for icons, patterns and backgrounds in CSS.
svg-to-css.howTo: Paste your SVG or drop an .svg file onto the field. Pick the output format, check the preview and copy the result into your CSS.

faq.q1: Why URL encoding instead of Base64?
faq.a1: SVG is text. URL encoding only escapes a few characters, so the result is usually about a third smaller than Base64 and compresses better with gzip.
faq.q2: Why does my SVG not show up?
faq.a2: An SVG used as an image needs the attribute xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on its root element. The converter adds it if it is missing. External images and fonts inside the SVG are not loaded in CSS backgrounds.
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser, nothing is sent to a server.

css-to-svg.name: CSS to SVG
css-to-svg.title: CSS to SVG converter
css-to-svg.description: Extract the SVG from a CSS data URI, URL-encoded or Base64, and get clean SVG code back.
css-to-svg.whatIs: Many stylesheets contain icons and patterns as embedded SVG data URIs. This converter finds the first SVG data URI in your CSS, decodes it and shows the original SVG code, so you can edit it again.
css-to-svg.howTo: Paste a CSS rule, a url() value or the bare data URI. The SVG appears next to it, ready to copy or to download as an .svg file.

faq.a1: Data URIs with the type image/svg+xml, URL-encoded or Base64, in double quotes, single quotes or without quotes.
faq.q2: My CSS contains several images. Which one do I get?
faq.a2: The first SVG data URI. To get another one, paste only the rule you need.
faq.q3: Is the SVG safe to use?
faq.a3: The preview shows the SVG as an image, so scripts in it never run here. Check SVG from unknown sources before you embed it directly in your own pages.

svg-to-base64.name: SVG to Base64
svg-to-base64.title: SVG to Base64 converter
svg-to-base64.description: Encode SVG as Base64 for data URIs, CSS, HTML or JSON.
svg-to-base64.whatIs: Base64 turns any file into plain letters and digits. For SVG it is useful wherever only Base64 is accepted, for example in some email clients, JSON APIs or older tools.
svg-to-base64.howTo: Paste your SVG or choose a file. Pick data URI, Base64 only, CSS or an HTML tag and copy the result.

faq.a1: For CSS, URL encoding is usually shorter. Base64 is about 33 percent larger than the original but works everywhere a data URI is accepted.
faq.a2: Yes. The SVG is encoded as UTF-8 before the Base64 step, so special characters survive the round trip.
faq.a3: Inputs up to 5 MB are converted directly in your browser. Large data URIs slow pages down, so keep embedded graphics small.

base64-to-svg.name: Base64 to SVG
base64-to-svg.title: Base64 to SVG converter
base64-to-svg.description: Decode Base64 or a data URI back into readable SVG code.
base64-to-svg.whatIs: Embedded SVGs are hard to read as Base64. This converter decodes the string, checks that it really is an SVG and shows you the code and a preview.
base64-to-svg.howTo: Paste raw Base64, a data URI or a whole CSS line. Copy the SVG code or download it as a file.

faq.q1: Do I need the data:image/svg+xml prefix?
faq.a1: No. Raw Base64 and complete data URIs both work, line breaks and spaces are ignored.
faq.q2: Why do I get an error?
faq.a2: Either the string is not valid Base64 or the decoded content is not an SVG. For PNG, JPG and other images, use the Base64 to image converter.
faq.a3: No. Decoding happens locally in your browser.

image-to-base64.name: Image to Base64
image-to-base64.title: Image to Base64 converter
image-to-base64.description: Convert PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG into a Base64 data URI for CSS and HTML.
image-to-base64.whatIs: A Base64 data URI contains the whole image as text. You can paste it straight into CSS, HTML or an email template without hosting a separate file.
image-to-base64.howTo: Choose an image, drop it onto the field or paste it from the clipboard. Pick an output format and copy the result.

faq.a1: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG up to 5 MB. The type is detected from the file content, not from the file name.
faq.a2: For small images such as icons or placeholders. Larger images are better served as separate files, because Base64 adds about 33 percent and cannot be cached on its own.
faq.a3: No. The image stays on your device, the conversion runs in your browser.

base64-to-image.name: Base64 to image
base64-to-image.title: Base64 to image converter
base64-to-image.description: Turn Base64 or a data URI back into a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG file.
base64-to-image.whatIs: Found an image as Base64 in CSS, HTML or an API response? This converter decodes it, detects the real image type from the content and lets you save it as a file.
base64-to-image.howTo: Paste the Base64 string or data URI. Check the preview, then download the image.

faq.a1: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG. Other content, such as HTML or scripts, is rejected.
faq.q2: The data URI says PNG, but I get a JPG. Why?
faq.a2: The converter trusts the content, not the label. If they differ, you get the file type that matches the actual data.
faq.a3: Yes, decoded images can be up to 5 MB. Everything runs in your browser.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Musterli is built to collect as little data as possible. There is no account, no cookies and no cross-site tracking. Motifs and images are computed in your browser. Here you can find out which data is still processed, and why.

controller.heading: Controller
paragraphs: The operator named below is responsible for processing your personal data on this website. You can reach them by email with questions about privacy and with your requests.

law.heading: Applicable law
paragraphs: This policy follows the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP). Where the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies, for example because you visit the website from the EU or EEA, its requirements apply as well.

Where the GDPR requires a legal basis, we process data based on our legitimate interest in running the website securely, reliably and without errors (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). If you write to us, the legal basis is answering your request (Art. 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR).

hosting.heading: Hosting with Cloudflare
paragraphs: The website runs on Cloudflare Workers, a service of Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. Cloudflare delivers the pages through a worldwide network of data centers and protects them against attacks.

When you open a page, Cloudflare processes technically necessary data: your IP address, date and time, the requested address, the previously visited page (referrer), and your browser and operating system (user agent). This data is used for delivery, security and troubleshooting. We do not analyze it to identify you.
Data may be transferred to the USA and other countries in the process; see the section “Transfers abroad”.

analytics.heading: Statistics with Cloudflare Web Analytics
paragraphs: To understand which pages are used and how fast they load, we use Cloudflare Web Analytics. The service works without cookies and without local storage in your browser and, according to Cloudflare, creates no profiles and no fingerprint of your device.

A small script from static.cloudflareinsights.com sends the following to Cloudflare when a page is opened: the page address without query parameters, the previously visited page, browser, operating system and device type, the country (derived from the IP address), and load times and page speed metrics. We only see aggregated numbers, never individual visits.
The script only runs on the public website, not on preview or test environments.

errors.heading: Error reports with Sentry
paragraphs: To find and fix bugs, we use Sentry, a service of Functional Software, Inc., 45 Fremont Street, 8th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA. We chose the EU data region: error reports are stored in data centers in the EU (Germany).

Sentry is only loaded when an error occurs on a page. An error report contains the error message, the location in the program code, browser and operating system, the page address without query parameters and without the part after the # sign, and the time. There are no cookies, no recording of your session and no performance tracking.

Your IP address has to be processed technically for the transfer. We configured Sentry not to store IP addresses or any other personal details. Error reports are deleted automatically when the retention period of our Sentry plan ends.

cookies.heading: No cookies, only local settings
paragraphs: Musterli sets no cookies. So you don’t have to pick your theme and your preferred export format every time, your browser keeps these two settings in local storage (localStorage). They stay on your device, are not sent to us, and you can delete them at any time in your browser settings.

Designs you save, the editor’s automatic drafts and your Brand Kit (palettes, logos, shapes) are kept in your browser’s database (IndexedDB). This data also stays on your device and is not sent to us. You can delete it in Musterli itself or, like the settings, in your browser settings.

local.heading: Images stay in your browser
paragraphs: When you load an image or file into a converter or create a color palette from an image, the file is processed only in your browser. It is neither uploaded nor stored, and it is gone as soon as you close the tab.

Images you use in a tool (for example your own motif in Seamless Patterns) or add to your Brand Kit are never uploaded either. If you save the design or the Brand Kit, they stay in your browser (see above). They only leave your device when you export a file yourself, and they are never part of a share link.

liveView.heading: Live view in the Screenshot Beautifier
paragraphs: If you turn on the live view in the Screenshot Beautifier, your browser loads the website whose address you entered directly from its server, in an isolated frame. Like on any visit, that website receives technically necessary data such as your IP address, date and time and your user agent, and its own privacy policy applies. Nothing passes through Musterli, and we do not learn the address.

“Take this view” lets your browser capture a picture of this tab after you allow it. The capture stops right away and is processed only in your browser. The picture is treated like an uploaded screenshot: it stays on your device and is never part of a share link.

share.heading: Share links
paragraphs: A share link holds your motif’s settings in the part of the address after the # sign. Your browser does not send this part to our server. Anyone with the link can see the motif. Colors derived from an image are not included in the link.

contact.heading: Contact by email
paragraphs: If you write to us, we process your email address and the content of your message to answer your request. We delete the message once it is resolved and no legal retention obligation applies.

donations.heading: Donations
paragraphs: Musterli is free and funded by voluntary donations. We use Ko-fi for this, a service of Ko-fi Labs Limited, based in the United Kingdom. Musterli itself accepts no payments and receives neither payment nor account details from you.

On the home page we show a donate button from Ko-fi. For this, your browser loads a script, a stylesheet and a logo from storage.ko-fi.com when you open the home page. Ko-fi receives technically necessary data such as your IP address, date and time, the page address and your user agent. We deliberately do not load Google fonts for it. The button itself sets no cookies on Musterli and uses no local storage.

Only when you click the button does the donation form from ko-fi.com open in an embedded window. The “Support” page also links directly to Ko-fi. Ko-fi is responsible for everything that happens in the donation form or on ko-fi.com. Ko-fi and its payment providers may set cookies there, and Ko-fi’s privacy policy applies. Ko-fi may tell us the amount donated and any details you explicitly choose to share with us.
We embed the donate button because we have a legitimate interest in offering a simple way to support Musterli (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

transfer.heading: Transfers abroad
paragraphs: Cloudflare and Sentry are based in the USA. Cloudflare may also process data in other countries where it operates data centers. For the USA we rely on the providers’ certification under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, and on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses in the providers’ data processing agreements.
We store Sentry error reports in the EU. Access from the USA, for example by the provider’s support, still cannot be ruled out.

Ko-fi is based in the United Kingdom. The European Commission and the Swiss Federal Council have recognised the United Kingdom as providing adequate data protection. Ko-fi and its payment providers may also process data in the USA.

retention.heading: Retention
paragraphs: We keep personal data only as long as needed for its purpose or required by law. We only see statistics in aggregated form. The providers delete technical logs and error reports automatically according to their retention periods.

rights.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your personal data and to have incorrect data corrected. You can ask us to delete data or restrict its processing, and you can object to processing. Where applicable, you also have the right to receive your data in a common format.
To do so, write to us at the email address above. We may ask for proof of your identity.
You can also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority: in Switzerland the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), in the EU the authority of your country of residence.

free.heading: Free and without warranty

We provide Musterli as it is. We do our best to keep everything working and the site online, but we cannot promise it. Nor do we promise that results are free of errors or fit for a particular purpose. Check your exports yourself before you use them, for example colour contrast, resolution or print requirements. As far as the law permits, we are not liable for damage arising from the use of Musterli, for example lost designs or lost profits. For damage caused intentionally or through gross negligence, we are liable as the law provides.

local.heading: Everything runs in your browser
paragraphs: Musterli computes, exports and saves right in your browser. Saved designs, drafts and your Brand Kit live on your device only, not on our servers. Images and logos you upload never leave your device.

That is why backups are up to you: if you clear your browser data or switch devices, locally saved designs are gone. You can back them up with the file export in “My designs” and in the Brand Kit. Everything else about data is explained in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

exports.heading: You may use your exports freely
paragraphs: Graphics, animations, colour palettes and code (for example SVG, CSS or Tailwind) that you create with Musterli are yours to use freely: privately and commercially, modified or unmodified, in your own projects and in work for others. Attribution is not required, though of course it is welcome.

Musterli makes no claims on your exports. To the extent we hold any rights in them at all, we waive them irrevocably, worldwide and as far as the law allows. In spirit this matches the Creative Commons “CC0 1.0 Universal” dedication. The same applies to the gradients and colour palettes in our collections.

This waiver only covers what you export. The website itself, meaning its texts, design, program code and the Musterli name and logo, remains protected. Because the generators work with settings and randomness, others may create identical or similar graphics. We therefore cannot give you an exclusive right to a motif.

uploads.heading: Your content
paragraphs: You are responsible for the content you use in Musterli, for example logos, images, shapes or lettering. Only use content you hold the necessary rights to, and nothing unlawful.

Musterli acquires no rights in your content, which is processed in your browser only. If an export contains your own content or that of third parties, their rights continue to apply to those parts. The waiver above does not cover them.

fair.heading: Fair use
paragraphs: Use Musterli in a way that keeps it working for everyone else. In particular, automated mass requests (for example by bots or scrapers), attempts to get around security measures, and anything that disrupts operation are not allowed.
In case of misuse we may restrict or block access, also without prior notice.

donations.heading: Donations
paragraphs: Musterli is funded by voluntary donations. A donation is a gift: it gets you no extra features and no claim to any particular service, and Musterli stays the same for everyone.

Donations go through an external provider, currently Ko-fi. Musterli itself accepts no payments. The provider’s terms and privacy policy apply to your donation. More on the <support>Support Musterli</support> page.

GradientPage.openEditorHint: Change angle, shape and colors, then export as CSS, SVG or PNG.
GradientPage.colorsLead: The color stops of the gradient. Click a value to copy it.
GradientPage.cssLead: Paste the lines into your element's rule. The first line is a fallback color, the second the gradient for every browser, the third interpolates in OKLCH for modern browsers.
GradientPage.variantsLead: The same colors in other generators. Each card opens the editor with these colors.
GradientPage.colorToolsLead: Turn the color stops into a palette or a full color scale.
GradientPage.howTo: Copy the CSS into the rule of the element that should carry the gradient, for example a section, a card or a button. For text on top, pick a text color with enough contrast on every color stop; the values next to the colors help you with that. In the editor you change angle, shape and easing and can also export the gradient as an image.

PalettePage.colorsLead: Click a value to copy it. Each swatch shows its value in the text color that reads best on it.
